questions.question: Over-the-counter medication:

options.text: Does not create any safety risks for drivers.
Is not mentioned in any driving under the influence laws.
Can reduce a driver's ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can reduce a driver's ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that hurt driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine work properly:
questions.correctAnswerText: In all weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze helps your engine even in hot weather.

questions.question: If a truck has one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: If a tractor-trailer has a trailer brake hand valve, you can use it to stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without any traffic violations.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road driving test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals, following all traffic laws, and finishing without any accidents or violations.

questions.question: When checking springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure torsion springs are not damaged.
Use glue to fix cracked leaf springs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use glue to fix cracked leaf springs.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs and coil springs. If your vehicle has torsion bars or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are fastened securely.

questions.question: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials exist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nine
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into nine classes. Each class describes the type of risk that material presents.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: Emergency exits are hard to open.
Emergency exit warning devices work correctly.
Emergency exits cannot be reached from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency exit warning devices work correctly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that all emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, be in good condition, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid driving in fog. If you must drive through fog, slow down, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, and turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels past the rear boundary line.
Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
At an angle within the parking space boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked straight and within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Text on your cell phone instead of calling.
Do not use your cell phone.
Turn up the volume on your cell phone ringer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use your cell phone.
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic requires your full attention. You should avoid all distractions, including cell phone use.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil from vehicles on the road. This creates a slippery surface that is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver is using their high beam headlights?

options.text: Flash your high beam lights to signal them to switch to low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until they pass.
Pull to the side of the road until they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until they pass.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright lights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What must the driver's seat of a bus have?

options.text: A storage pocket on the left side.
A storage pocket on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat belt.
questions.explanation: A bus driver's seat must have a seat belt. The driver should always wear it.

questions.question: When you start the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: When checking the engine before a trip, start it and listen for any strange or unusual sounds.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following must you NOT do?

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic laws, and complete the test without accidents or violations.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure while traveling?

options.text: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure.

questions.question: What is an encroachment during a vehicle control skills test?

options.text: The vehicle touching or crossing over a boundary line.
A driver making one forward movement.
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.
The vehicle stalling while changing gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching or crossing over a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A large amount, like a big puddle

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. This can happen with even a small amount of water.

questions.question: Why is it important to inspect your vehicle before a trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: To ensure safety.
questions.explanation: Vehicle inspections before every trip are required by law to keep you and others safe on the road.
